source_text:
Ἔξεστι δὲ τοῦ φαρμάκου τοῦδε καὶ ἐφ' ἡσυχίας πεῖραν λαβεῖν, καὶ
θαυμάσαι πόση ἀπὸ τοῦδε ἰσχύς ἐστιν καὶ ἐν πολέμῳ κρείττων βελῶν. Καταπέσοι δ'
ἂν ἄλλως ἵππος, θαλαττίας χελώνης ῥανθεὶς τοὺς μυκτῆρας τῇ χολῇ, καί, πρὸς τῶν
ἰδίων ἀπογνωσθείς, ἡμέτερόν ἐστι κέρδος. Ἀναστήσεται γάρ, εἰ κρόκον σμύρναν τε
ἅμα κρίνῳ μίξας ἐπίσης τοῦ ῥύγχους ἐπαφῆσαί τις αὐτοῦ· ἀναστήσονται
καταπεσόντες καὶ ὀρεῖς. Ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ ὁ τοῦ καρπάσου ὀπὸς μᾶλλον ἵπποις
θανατήσιος. Ἀποθάνοιεν δ' ἂν καὶ φαλαγγίοις καὶ σαλαμάνδρᾳ περιπετεῖς τε
γενόμενοι κισσοῦ τε δακρύῳ καὶ στύρακος χυλῷ. Ἀδικοῦνται δὲ καὶ τῷ ἐξ ἀφέδρου
ῥάκους καπνῷ. Ταυτὶ μὲν οὖν ἄλλως εἰρήσθω. ∆ερκυλλίδας δὲ ὁ Λακεδαιμόνιος, τῇ
τῶν ἀντιπάλων ἵππῳ πεζὴν φάλαγγα προσαγαγών, ἐν τῷ πλινθίῳ καὶ ἀντινώτους
τάξας εἰς βάθος, παρήγγειλεν ἑζομένοις ὑπ' ἀσπίδι τοῖς κατόπιν ὅ τι τάχος τοῖς
ἐγχειριδίοις βόθρους ὀρύσσειν· ἔπειτ' εἰς τὸ μέσον ἀνῆγε τοὺς ὁπλίτας· καὶ ἦσαν
ἔρυμα· οἱ γὰρ βόθροι τοῖς ἱππεῦσι πολεμιώτατοι.
pass_a_gloss: It is-possible also of this drug even at leisure to-take a trial, and to-wonder how-much strength there is from this, and in war better than missiles. A horse would-fall otherwise, having-been-sprinkled at the nostrils with the bile of a sea-turtle, and, having-been-given-up by his own, it is our gain. For he will-stand-up if someone mixing saffron and myrrh together with lily equally apply it of his snout; fallen mules also will-stand-up. But the juice of karpasos is more death-dealing to horses. They would-also-die having-become-entangled with phalangia and with a salamander, and with ivy-tear and storax-juice. They are-also-harmed by the smoke from a menstrual rag. Let these things then have-been-said otherwise. Dercyllidas the Lacedaemonian, having-brought an infantry phalanx against the opponents' horse, in the brick-shape and having-stationed them back-to-back into depth, ordered those behind sitting under shield to-dig pits with the daggers as-fast-as-possible; then he led the hoplites into the middle; and they were a defense; for the pits are most-hostile to the horsemen.
pass_b_english: It is possible also to take a trial of this drug even at leisure, and to wonder how much strength there is from it, and in war better than missiles. A horse would fall otherwise, the nostrils sprinkled with the bile of a sea-turtle; and, given up by his own, it is our gain. For he will stand up if someone mix saffron and myrrh together with lily equally and apply it to his snout. Fallen mules will also stand up. But the juice of karpasos is more death-dealing to horses. They would also die if they became entangled with phalangia and with a salamander, and with ivy-tear and storax-juice. They are harmed too by the smoke from a menstrual rag. Let these things have been said otherwise.

Dercyllidas the Lacedaemonian, having brought an infantry phalanx against the opponents' horse, stationing them in the brick-shape and back-to-back in depth, ordered those behind, sitting under the shield, to dig pits with the daggers as fast as possible. Then he led the hoplites into the middle; and they were a defense. For the pits are most hostile to the horsemen.

choices.english: the smoke from a menstrual rag
choices.why: ἄφεδρος is menses; the lock's harm is smoke from that rag, not 'a sitting-cloth' or a generic dirty rag.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
